statement: Once a record's own explicit identity anchor has been reconciled by a resolver that itself performed the full, authenticated principal-resolution walk (auth_user_id -> root_identity -> kybe_id), a DOWNSTREAM consumer that only needs 'what root/kybe does this record name' must read that record's own anchor columns directly and must NOT re-run the stricter auth-user-disambiguation walk a second time. Re-deriving an already-resolved principal re-litigates a completed decision and can incorrectly refuse on a totally unrelated historical condition (e.g. sibling identity rows under other logins) that has nothing to do with the record's own named anchor. The stricter, authentication-sensitive resolver stays exactly as strict as it needs to be for its OWN callers (fresh session-grade resolution); a narrower, separate resolver is added for the downstream 'read the already-settled answer' question rather than weakening the strict one.
classification: Engineering/architectural invariant (candidate causal pattern) about re-derivation vs reuse of an already-resolved identity anchor, in the Chrysalis Homecoming (CFS-023) constitutional anchoring repair.

occurrences.site: services/agents/repairDelegationAnchor.ts (fixed 2026-08-15) — previously called resolvePassportPrincipalById, now calls resolvePassportExplicitAnchor
occurrences.defect: repairDelegationAnchor resolved a sponsor Passport's principal via resolvePassportPrincipalById, which re-runs auth-user sibling-root disambiguation even when the Passport's own root_identity_id/kybe_identity_id had ALREADY been reconciled (by services/passport/legacyPassportLinkageRepair.ts, itself resolved from the caller's authenticated session). The re-derivation correctly refused the moment the resolved kybe also had unrelated historical sibling root_identity rows under other auth users — a real condition, but irrelevant to what the Passport itself names as its root.

canaries.assertion: resolvePassportExplicitAnchor resolves a Passport's root/kybe purely from its own columns, structurally never issuing a kybe-wide sibling scan (a single root_identity query by primary key only), and succeeds even when the resolved kybe has multiple sibling root_identity rows under different auth users seeded in the fake table.

The 'LIVE REGRESSION' canary reproduces the exact live condition (sponsor Passport with a valid explicit anchor, kybe with unrelated sibling auth roots) and confirms repairDelegationAnchor succeeds using only the Passport's own recorded root, never touching root_identity directly.

notes: Does NOT weaken resolvePassportPrincipalById or resolveAuthUserForKybe — both are unchanged and remain correct for their existing authentication-sensitive callers (wallet/WorldID/passkey connection flows), which genuinely need session-grade auth-user certainty from zero prior context.

The multi-auth-user-under-one-kybe condition itself (the operator's own account spanning more than one Supabase login under one personhood) is NOT resolved by this invariant or its resolution record — it remains a real, separate PRD-PAG-001 Amendment A §A.5 'Passport consolidation' question, deliberately out of scope here per explicit operator instruction.

Relationship to CI-2026-08-15-PRINCIPAL-RESOLUTION-NEVER-VIA-PERSONA-DID-001: that invariant governs how a principal is FIRST established (from auth_user_id, never from a persona-owned DID-shaped field). This invariant governs REUSE of a principal already established — once settled and recorded on a specific row, a downstream consumer of that row reads it directly rather than re-running the establishment walk. Complementary, not overlapping: one is about origination, the other about propagation.
